expectations.name: correct-but-terse-is-left-alone
expected_behavior: Runs the checklist and finds that no item fires
Leaves the comment byte-for-byte unchanged — no padding, no restating the signature
Reports no change line for it; shortness alone is not a defect

expectations.name: adds-only-confirmable-facts
expected_behavior: Fires the missing-fact checklist item for the slice mutation, which the body proves
Documents that mutation, naming what the caller must not assume about the slice afterwards
Writes nothing about concurrency: the absence of a mutex is not evidence of a guarantee either way, and "not safe for concurrent use" would be a conclusion about code nobody wrote

expectations.name: directives-and-interface-method-godoc
expected_behavior: Leaves both directive comments byte-for-byte unchanged and lists them as never-touch items in the plan
Plans the `Read` godoc for removal as unremarkable — it would be kept, naming the surprise, only if `Read` broke or exceeded the `io.Reader` contract
Writes nothing before approval: the plan is the run's only output on that turn, and every `.go` file's mtime is unchanged until the approval turn — check the files, not the promise

expectations.name: terse-output
expected_behavior: No narration: the reply is the changes made, the Verify result, and the verdict. A one-line note that no language server was available is a fact, not narration
Lists changes made as `file:Symbol — item`, plus flagged and never-touched items, each stated once
No closing restatement of the edits it just listed

expectations.name: line-target-resolves-to-its-item
expected_behavior: States the resolved kind (line) and the item it resolved to: the inline comments of `(*Svc).Flush`'s body — the innermost item containing line 42, not the enclosing declaration's godoc, which `func=Flush` would reach
Touches only the item the line resolves to: every other function in the file is byte-identical after the run, whether or not it had a defect
Presents no plan; a line target is a single item, so it runs the loop straight through
Deletes `// increment i` as a comment that only restates the code

expectations.name: module-mode-with-fanout-and-filter
expected_behavior: The plan lists items from `svc` and `api` only; every other package is reported as skipped
Fans out one worker per in-scope package and merges their reports — each worker's per-package report survives on disk, so the fan-out is visible rather than asserted
No comment anywhere claims `Router` is or is not safe for concurrent use — the absence of a mutex is not evidence either way
The parent re-checks each worker's added or changed comment against the checklist before merging, and reverts any fact the code does not establish, saying so in the report
Reports the Verify result in the reply — which packages were gate-checked and that `gofmt -l` and `go build` passed

expectations.name: side-effect-is-not-a-surprise
expected_behavior: Removes `(*fileSink).Write`'s godoc as unremarkable: performing its own contract is not a surprise, however many side effects it takes
Keeps `(*teeSink).Write`'s godoc and expands it to name the surprise — the second write, and the success return that hides its failure
Does not treat "has a side effect" as sufficient on its own to keep a comment, or both would be kept
